title: Experimental Study on Spray Activation in a Containment Atmosphere with Superheated Steam Conditions during a Design Basis Accident
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents experimental results on large-scale containment thermal-hydraulics driven by the combined effects of steam injection and spray activation under a postulated design basis accident scenario, such as a main steam line break. The experimental campaign consisted of two experiments, identified as P1A1_5 and P1A1_6, which form part of the P1A1 series conducted within the OECD/NEA PANDA project to investigate PWR containment spray systems. The experiments were conducted in the facility, which consists of a large-scale cylindrical vessel. Initial conditions involved pressurization with air and steam up to 2.5 bar under superheated conditions. The spray system was activated using a single nozzle. The experiments were divided into three phases: steam injection only, combined steam and spray injection, and spray only injection. The results show that during containment depressurization, steam remains superheated above the spray nozzle, whereas below the nozzle the measured fluid temperature closely follows the saturation temperature. This behavior may be associated with enhanced condensation near the vessel wall and possible spray-induced flow recirculation. Upon spray activation, pressure and temperature gradients below the spray nozzle decrease more rapidly over time than during Phase 2, possibly reflecting spray-induced mixing and droplet dynamics.

title: Impact of residual nuclides on the transmutation of Np and Am in a lead-cooled fast reactor
abstract: Partitioning and Transmutation (P&T) is recognized as an effective strategy for mitigating the burden associated with the geological disposal of minor actinide (MA) nuclides. This study investigates the impact of three types of residual nuclides, namely, rare earth elements (REs), uranium, and plutonium, that remain in MA fuels during the partitioning process. Based on a 500 MW th lead-cooled fast reactor (LFR) developed using OpenMC, the effects of these residuals on the transmutation performance of 237 Np, 241 Am and 243 Am are systematically analyzed. The results reveal that the effective delayed neutron fraction varies non-monotonically within the 0-50 wt.% residual nuclide content range, and no significant decrease is observed. Spectral analysis demonstrates that RE 2 O 3 (rare earth oxide) and UO 2 induce spectrum softening, whereas PuO 2 hardens the spectrum. Transmutation calculations further show that for all three MAs, both the transmutation rates and capture-to-fission ratios increase approximately linearly with an increasing RE 2 O 3 and UO 2 content, whereas they decrease with an increase in PuO 2 content. This research elucidates the distinct mechanisms of these residuals in LFRs, providing a foundational basis for developing transmutation strategies for impure MA fuels.

title: Experimental study on flow patterns and pressure oscillation characteristics of vertical upward steam jets at low water temperatures
abstract: Experiments were conducted to examine flow-regime transitions and pressure responses of vertically upward steam jets at low water temperatures (0–50 °C) and steam mass fluxes of 40–550 kg/(m 2 ·s). By combining high-speed imaging with high-frequency dynamic-pressure measurements, a flow-regime map was constructed. Within the investigated parameter range, seven regimes were identified and their observed operating regions were mapped. The maximum positive pressure excursion, p max , was used as a descriptive peak metric over each displayed time interval. For the three displayed 5-s chugging records, p max increased from 4.94 to 20.53 kPa as pool-water temperature increased from 0 to 20 °C. Among the displayed 50-ms records, hemispherical condensation oscillation reached 88.53 kPa, ellipsoidal condensation oscillation reached 149.85 kPa, and the stable-jet cases ranged from 5.16 to 10.56 kPa. These values are single-run, non-duration-normalized maxima.

title: Effects of Activation Energy and Joule Heating on Reactive MHD Micropolar Nanofluid Flow Over a Permeable Stretching Sheet
abstract: In this work, the effect of combined Joule heating and activation energy on steady magnetohydrodynamic micropolar nanofluid flow along a permeable stretching surface is investigated. The novelty of this model is the coupling of micropolar microrotational physics with thermal radiation, viscous dissipation, Dufour diffusion, and temperature-dependent chemical kinetics. The governing nonlinear partial differential equations are converted to a set of coupled ordinary differential equations by similarity transformations and then numerically solved by the fourth-order Adams-Moulton method with a shooting technique. The results indicate that there was significant improvement in the thermal field by the Joule heating effect, which caused the surface heat transfer rate to decrease by 4.17% due to the Joule heating. On the other hand, for a higher activation energy, chemical reaction kinetics decreases, and thus, the number of nanoparticles increases as the rate of mass transfer decreases by 15.02%. Moreover, the effect of viscous dissipation and thermal radiation increases the thermal boundary layer thickness while the cross-diffusion transport of the species is dominated by Brownian motion and thermophoresis. These insights provide practical design mechanisms for optimizing advanced nanofluid thermal management systems in high-temperature engineering applications.

title: Exploring the effects of dual-layered Cr/Nb coating thickness on the corrosion and annealing response characteristics of an accident-tolerant Zr fuel cladding material
abstract: Cr-coated Zr alloys are accident-tolerant fuel (ATF) cladding materials that offer practical solutions to nuclear challenges due to their inherent benefits. Nonetheless, drawbacks remain, including Cr-Zr interdiffusion, which accelerates coating degradation, especially where the role of interlayer coating thickness is not clearly defined. In this study, an Nb interlayer barrier is fabricated between a Cr topcoat and Zircaloy-4 to investigate how corrosion and annealing response characteristics change with varying thickness. Annealing at 1200 °C for 5 min led to microcrack formation at the coating/alloy interfaces, interfacial voids (in thicker coatings), and adhesion loss (in thinner coatings). This was followed by an average thickness loss of up to 1.1 μm for the former and 2.3 μm for the latter. The present study was conducted under thermal conditions simulating a near-serious accident scenario to observe potential interfacial changes at a relatively accelerated rate. While high-temperature electrochemistry remains relatively unexplored in nuclear research as an approach to studying coolant chemistry, the conditions for the present electrochemistry and Zr-release studies were chosen only to test corrosion performance, and not to simulate reactor conditions. The long-term research objective is to develop safe, reliable ATF cladding materials for use in light-water reactors (LWRs) under varying conditions.

title: Surrogate-based engineering evaluation and service-life enhancement of a pleated 316 L metal-fiber cartridge for lead‑bismuth coolant purification
abstract: Corrosion-product control in lead‑bismuth eutectic (LBE) coolant loops is important for maintaining hydraulic reliability, reducing impurity accumulation, and extending the service life of purification components. However, engineering-scale data on the filtration efficiency, dust-holding capacity, and pressure-drop evolution of pleated metal-fiber cartridges for LBE systems remain limited. In this study, a pleated 316 L sintered metal-fiber cartridge was experimentally evaluated using a water-SiO 2 surrogate system, and the applicability of the surrogate was assessed through mechanism-based similarity analysis. The results show that both the surrogate and the target PbBi-Fe3O4 system operate in the creeping-flow regime (Re f < 1), with comparable Peclet numbers and interception-dominated capture, supporting the use of the surrogate for engineering performance evaluation within the investigated regime. Under representative operating conditions, the clean cartridge exhibited high instantaneous removal efficiency (>95%) and a dust-holding capacity of 1668 g/m 2 at a terminal pressure drop of 300 kPa. Continuous segmented regression revealed a two-stage pressure-drop/loading relationship with a transition at approximately 1027–1050 g/m 2 , corresponding to a shift from pleat-internal loading to outer-surface cake growth. This transition provides a practical maintenance indicator for cartridge replacement. Structural optimization showed that reducing the packing density of the sintered medium increased dust-holding capacity by 6.86%, while introducing an outer loose-fiber layer further delayed rapid pressure-drop growth. The best configuration, a 3 mm-compressed coating with an 8 μm fiber diameter, increased the corrected dust-holding capacity from 2048 to 3052 g/m 2 , corresponding to a 49.05% improvement. The present work establishes a surrogate-based engineering framework for evaluating and optimizing pleated metal-fiber cartridges for corrosion-product removal in LBE coolant purification systems.

title: Experimental and numerical study on aerosol mass concentration attenuation in reactor containment during LBB events
abstract: Under Leak-Before-Break (LBB) accident conditions, containment ventilation systems can operate under elevated air exchange conditions, introducing forced convection that modifies aerosol transport behavior. Large internal structures in engineering-scale compartments further disturb the flow field and generate spatially heterogeneous flow and turbulence structures. Many existing aerosol attenuation and deposition models were developed and validated either for sealed, quiescent environments dominated by natural convection, or for obstacle-free chambers under low-to-moderate ventilation rates. Their applicability to LBB-relevant conditions therefore remains uncertain. This study investigates aerosol attenuation in a mechanically ventilated compartment with representative nuclear-island obstacle layouts at an air change rate of 12 h −1 , intended to represent compact containment layouts adopted in integral pressurized water reactor and small modular reactor concepts. Experiments were combined with numerical simulations comparing an Eulerian approach incorporating the Lai–Nazaroff deposition formulation and a Lagrangian Discrete Phase Model with Discrete Random Walk (DPM–DRW) framework. The measured average total aerosol removal rate was 25.4 h −1 , of which deposition contributed 13.4 h −1 . This deposition component exceeds values commonly reported under conventional indoor ventilation conditions and is comparable to the ventilation removal contribution. When coupled with a near-wall-resolving turbulence closure—specifically the Shear Stress Transport (SST) k–ω model—the DPM–DRW framework reproduced the observed attenuation trend with a predicted decay coefficient of 22.8 h −1 , within 10.2% of the measured 25.4 h −1 . By contrast, wall-function-based models (realizable k–ε) overpredicted removal by over a factor of two, while both the well-mixed single-zone model and the Lai–Nazaroff formulation systematically underestimated deposition-associated attenuation under the present geometric and flow conditions. These results indicate that deposition may remain an important removal mechanism even under elevated ventilation conditions in compactly arranged containment compartments. The findings suggest that conventional ventilation-dominated attenuation assumptions do not fully capture aerosol removal under the present conditions, and that deposition should therefore be considered when selecting an aerosol attenuation model for such compact configurations.

title: Structural improvement of tilting-pad thrust bearings in nuclear reactor coolant pumps based on thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication analysis
abstract: As a core supporting component of a nuclear main pump, the tilting-pad thrust bearing carries a large axial load, and its lubrication performance directly affects the operational reliability of the pump. This study develops a fluid–structure coupled thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication model for an oil-lubricated point-supported tilting-pad thrust bearing by considering the contact effect at the pad-back pivot. Within each physical time step, partitioned iterative coupling is implemented between the oil-film lubrication field and the thermoelastic deformation field of the pad. Based on this model, improved schemes for the pad pivot position and pad surface profile are determined, and the lubrication performance of the bearing under extreme accident conditions is evaluated. The results show that thermoelastic deformation of the pad significantly affects the distributions of oil-film pressure, film thickness, and temperature. Considering the maximum oil-film pressure, minimum oil-film thickness, and maximum oil-film temperature, the bearing investigated in this study exhibits the best comprehensive lubrication performance when the radial offset coefficient is 0.51, the circumferential offset coefficient is 0.57, and the height of the parabolic pad surface profile is 6 μm. The optimized structure also improves the pressure and film thickness distributions during coast-down condition, thereby enhancing the oil-film safety margin. This study provides a theoretical basis and numerical method support for thermal elastohydrodynamic lubrication analysis, structural parameter optimization, and transient shutdown safety evaluation of tilting-pad thrust bearings in reactor coolant pumps.

title: In-depth design and construction of an integrated thermal-hydraulic facility (INTALI) for a prismatic gas-cooled micro reactor
abstract: To support the development of an innovative gas-cooled micro reactor (GMR), an integrated thermal-hydraulic facility (INTALI) has been designed to investigate heat transfer and fluid behaviors under both prototypical operating conditions and representative accident scenarios, thus providing a basis for thermal-hydraulic code validation. The INTALI facility consists of a helium circulation loop and a test section containing a scaled-down simulated reactor and a passive core cooling system (PCCS). This paper aims to finalize the facility design and corresponding experimental methodology. Firstly, the overall configuration and layout of the apparatus were described. An analytical model was developed to predict the helium temperature distribution along the primary loop, which is critical to facility operational control and piping integrity. A pre-test calculation under nominal conditions indicates that all helium temperatures throughout the loop remain below the piping safety limit. Parametric calculations were performed to study the influences of both heating power and the flow rate ratio of the main flow to the protective flow. Secondly, the detailed structural designs of the test section were elaborated. Specific internal components within the reactor were designed, including tenon-mortise joints for fuel assembly alignment and core baffles to suppress bypass flow. Structural analysis confirms that incorporating four reinforced ribs improves the PCCS dome’s stiffness. The layout and the installation of thermocouples (TCs) within both the reactor and the PCCS were described. A comparative calculation demonstrates that the mixer effectively enhances mixing of the main and the protective flows, thus lowering the temperature at the reactor outlet. Thirdly, an experimental methodology was proposed to simulate an anticipated transient without scram (ATWS) accident initiated by loss of forced coolant. To incorporate the temperature-reactivity feedback, a computational module solving the neutron point kinetics model was developed and validated. Furthermore, dedicated data processing along with uncertainty analysis methods were formulated to derive key physical quantities from experimental measurements: 1) friction factor of helium through a coolant channel, 2) heat exchange rate between the reactor and the PCCS, and 3) convective heat transfer coefficient on the reactor pressure vessel (RPV) wall. Finally, the current status of facility construction and the planned testing program in the next stage are outlined.

title: Experimental study and modeling Investigation on counter-current flow limitation phenomenon in reactor downcomer with DVI injection
abstract: During the refilling phase of a large-break loss-of-coolant accident (LBLOCA), the large upward flow of steam generated in the core region enters the reactor downcomer, causing the cooling water to fail to descend into the reactor core in time. This results in counter-current flow limitation (CCFL). The passive safety injection system of the HPR1000 reactor incorporates direct vessel injection (DVI) technology in the reactor pressure vessel (RPV). DVI has different injection characteristics compared to traditional loop injection, leading to differences in the phenomena and processes during a LBLOCA. To investigate the gas–liquid two-phase characteristics of the CCFL behavior in the RPV downcomer section with DVI injection under LBLOCA conditions, an RPV integral test facility was designed and constructed based on scaling criteria and the design features of the prototype reactor, and experimental and modeling studies were then performed. Emergency core coolant (ECC) experimental data were obtained under different inlet ECC flow rates, core steam flow rates, etc. Based on these experimental results, a conservative analysis was performed using the LBLOCA-specific analysis code — CATHARE GB. The results indicate that lowering the axial height of the DVI nozzle and installing a DVI flow diversion structure can effectively suppress ECC bypass. The CATHARE GB model used in the analysis of the LBLOCA analysis with DVI injection is conservative, and the current reactor incorporates DVI technology within the RPV. The ECC design can maintain an adequate safety margin.

title: Critical heat flux prediction in water-cooled vertical tubes using fuzzy-clustering-assisted AdaBoost and random forest models
abstract: Accurate prediction of critical heat flux (CHF) in water-cooled vertical tubes is essential for thermal–hydraulic safety, yet many empirical and mechanistic methods are valid only within restricted operating ranges. This study evaluates whether fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering improves data-driven CHF prediction using 4,384 experimental observations from vertical round tubes. Six predictors were considered: tube diameter, heated length, pressure, mass flux, inlet subcooling, and exit quality. Elastic Net, k-nearest neighbors, random forests (RF), AdaBoost, FCM-assisted RF, and FCM-assisted AdaBoost were evaluated using a common fixed 70:30 training-test partition. Hyperparameters of the standalone models were optimized by five-fold cross-validation within the training set, whereas the FCM-assisted models used an internal fitting-validation split for joint optimization of the clustering and regression components. FCM membership values were used to decompose the CHF target without including CHF in the clustering inputs. FCM-assisted AdaBoost achieved the best test performance, with a relative root-mean-square error (rRMSE) of 18.1 % and a root-mean-square relative error (RMSRE) of 11.7 %. FCM markedly reduced the RMSRE of RF, from 65.9 % to 16.4 %, whereas the improvement over standalone AdaBoost was smaller (RMSRE: 16.1 % to 11.7 %). These results demonstrate that fuzzy pre-clustering can improve predictive performance for the present heterogeneous CHF dataset, although the physical interpretation of the resulting fuzzy partitions requires further investigation.

title: A buoyancy-adaptive reduced-order surrogate for heated rod-bundle transients using gauge-consistent deep orthogonal decomposition
abstract: Heated rod-bundle transients couple changes in flow rate, temperature, and buoyancy-driven secondary motion, making them difficult to represent with a fixed global reduced basis. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) works well for nearly linear forced-convection hydraulics, but the transverse structures that develop under mixed convection vary with the buoyancy state and require a basis that adapts to the operating condition. This study develops a buoyancy-adaptive reduced-order surrogate for transient rod-bundle thermal-hydraulics using gauge-consistent deep orthogonal decomposition (DOD). The surrogate reconstructs the three velocity components and the temperature field, and is coupled with a coolant-residence-time-based thermal-lag model with a data-calibrated prefactor and a quasi-steady hydraulic closure. It is evaluated against processed steady operating states and transient CFD simulations. Compared with a global POD using the same coefficient mapper, the DOD surrogate gives more accurate reconstructions of the buoyancy-sensitive transverse velocity components. Heated flow-decrease and flow-increase tests show that the surrogate captures the main axial-flow response and temperature evolution under both uniform and skewed heating conditions. These results demonstrate the benefit of buoyancy-adaptive reduced bases for reconstructing nonlinear transverse flow structures in heated rod-bundle transients and establish a practical route for extending real-time rod-bundle digital twins from isothermal hydraulics to heated buoyant transients.

title: Thermo-fluid characteristics at the points of onset of nucleate boiling and onset of significant void in vertical upward boiling flows
abstract: The onset of nucleate boiling (ONB) and the onset of significant void (OSV) are critical transition points that demarcate heat transfer regimes and govern the development of two-phase flow in subcooled boiling flows. Accurate prediction of these two characteristic points is of great significance for the thermal-hydraulic design and safety analysis of industrial heat exchange equipment, such as nuclear reactors and steam generators. This study focused on the local characteristics at the ONB and OSV points in vertical upward flow channels. Firstly, a low-pressure ONB experimental database covering various channel geometries (including circular tubes, rectangular channels, and rod bundles) was compiled, and the existing classical ONB prediction models were systematically evaluated. The results indicated that the existing models exhibited considerable scatter and significant deviations. To address this issue, a new ONB correlation was developed based on a correlation analysis of the active nucleation site density with dimensionless parameters. The developed correlation reduced the mean absolute relative deviation for wall superheat prediction at ONB to 19.7%, outperforming existing models. Secondly, for the OSV point, a comprehensive drift-flux model was employed to analyze the cross-sectional void fraction and its axial development rate, revealing an exponential correlation between these parameters and the modified dimensionless Sauter mean diameter. Furthermore, by incorporating a bubble layer thickness model, the local parameters of the bubble layer (i.e., bubble layer thickness and void fraction) at the OSV point were quantitatively characterized for both externally heated channels and internally heated annular channels, and corresponding predictive correlations were established. The results demonstrated that the average void fraction within the bubble layer remains essentially constant (approximately 0.1) in externally heated channels, whereas it increased exponentially with the cross-sectional void fraction in internally heated annular channels. The quantitative relationships established in this study addressed the deficiency of existing bubble coalescence-based OSV models in terms of closure relations for local parameters, thereby providing crucial theoretical support for the accurate modeling and engineering applications of subcooled boiling two-phase flows.

title: Design of a ZnO:Ga/SiPM array alpha detector for associated particle imaging
abstract: A compact associated alpha detector based on a ZnO:Ga scintillator coupled to a 121-channel SiPM array was proposed for associated particle imaging (API) applications. Monte Carlo simulations were performed to evaluate the detector response, position reconstruction capability, and timing performance. The simulation results show that scintillation light is shared among several neighboring SiPM channels, providing sufficient information for position and timing reconstruction. Position reconstruction was investigated using the COG method together with two-dimensional correction and CNN-based correction methods, achieving a spatial resolution better than 0.6 mm over most of the effective detection area. The timing performance was evaluated using an amplitude-weighted timing method combined with time-walk and flight-distance corrections, resulting in a timing resolution of 81.5 ps. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed detector concept and indicate that it is a promising SiPM-based solution for high-resolution API applications.

title: Biokinetic modelling of uranium retention and committed organ doses from groundwater ingestion in Chengalpattu District, Tamil Nadu, India
abstract: Groundwater samples collected from Chengalpattu District were analyzed for uranium using an LED fluorimeter. The measured values ranged between 0.02 μg L −1 and 2.814 μg L −1 , with an average concentration of 0.347 μg L −1 . All measured values were within the permissible limits recommended by the World Health Organization and the International Commission on Radiological Protection. The study evaluated organ-specific uranium retention and committed equivalent doses for adults under chronic ingestion conditions using a hair-based compartmental biokinetic model. The results further confirm the previously reported non-uniform distribution of uranium among human organs and tissues, with tissue-specific retention characteristics governing its accumulation and residence time. Skeletal tissues, particularly cortical and trabecular bone volumes, exhibited the highest accumulation due to the strong affinity of uranyl ions for phosphate groups in hydroxyapatite, leading to prolonged retention and the largest contribution to internal radiation dose. In contrast, soft tissues, gastrointestinal tract segments, kidneys, and liver showed lower retention due to faster transfer and elimination rates. The gastrointestinal tract acts as the primary entry pathway, while the kidneys and urinary bladder play key roles in uranium clearance. Excretion analysis indicates that faeces elimination is the dominant pathway, followed by urinary and minor hair excretion. The highest committed equivalent doses were observed in bone surfaces, followed by other soft tissues, the lower large intestine wall, kidneys, upper large intestine wall, small intestine wall, stomach wall, and liver. The overall effective dose is mainly influenced by skeletal retention; however, the estimated doses across all locations remain low and well within international safety limits. These findings suggest minimal radiological health risk from chronic uranium ingestion in the study area and demonstrate that the hair compartmental biokinetic model is a reliable tool for long-term exposure and risk assessment.

title: Reactor turbine coordinated control strategy for nuclear power plants based on thermal-mismatch
abstract: As power systems increasingly rely on flexibility resources, nuclear power will inevitably participate in grid load-following services. To improve the dynamic response performance of nuclear power plants during load-following operation, this paper proposes a reactor turbine coordinated control strategy based on thermal-mismatch analysis. The energy transfer characteristics between the primary and secondary loops of a pressurized water reactor (PWR) nuclear power plant operating in the “one reactor-two turbines” mode are analyzed. An energy-demand signal for the secondary loop and an energy-supply signal for the primary loop are constructed, and their difference is defined as the thermal-mismatch signal. By incorporating the pressure-power fitting coefficient and a control rod sensitivity coefficient, the thermal-mismatch signal is introduced into the reactor power control system as a feedforward signal. Furthermore, the heat-storage calculation methods of different regions in the once-through steam generator are analyzed. The boundary lengths are determined based on mass conservation on the secondary side, and the solution approach for the thermal storage coefficient is ultimately established. Finally, simulation results under operating conditions demonstrate that the strategy significantly improves the dynamic response of the primary-loop temperature during load variations. This paper provides an effective coordinated control scheme for enhancing the flexibility of PWR nuclear power plants in load-following operation.

title: Experimental study of a ten sodium heat pipe bundle array with various failure modes
abstract: Alkali metal heat pipes are key components for high-temperature heat removal in microreactors, where multiple heat pipes are embedded directly within the reactor core. Their collective thermal behavior, including interactions under off-normal conditions, remains insufficiently characterized. This study investigates the performance of a ten-heat-pipe array under a range of operating conditions, including simulated failure scenarios. Under steady-state operation, the vertical configuration produced more uniform vapor temperatures among the heat pipes, albeit with slightly longer startup times and marginally higher average operating temperatures compared to the horizontal orientation. System uncertainties associated with the heat pipe array configuration were quantified to support future model validation. Complete loss-of-function conditions were simulated by replacing one or two sodium heat pipes with empty tubes. In these cases, neighboring heat pipes redistributed the thermal load, resulting in increased local heat fluxes and a corresponding rise in system temperature. This localized overloading further amplified thermal stresses on adjacent heat pipes. The experimental results provide data for characterizing thermal interactions within heat-pipe arrays, offering useful guidance for the design of future experiments and the validation of numerical models used in the analysis of heat-pipe-cooled microreactor systems.

title: Void Avoidance in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks with Deformable Bi-Level Routing Attention-Based Multiagent Adaptive Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Routing Protocol
abstract: Underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs) have gained increasing importance in various military and civilian applications due to their ability to facilitate communication in challenging underwater environments. However, routing in UASNs faces unique challenges stemming from the harsh characteristics of underwater acoustic communication caused by water currents and node mobility. This work suggests a comprehensive routing framework that uniquely integrates void avoidance with intelligent, deep reinforcement learning–based routing techniques.The contribution from this research is the performance of void avoidance and routing for the effective transmission. Specifically, a novel HH-VBF (hop-by-hop vector-based forwarding) method is employed to detect and eliminate the void nodes, thereby enhancing reliability and reducing packet loss. Furthermore, the proposed deformable bi-level routing attention-based multi-agent adaptive deep deterministic policy gradient (DBRAMADDPG) algorithm, optimized using the improved nuclear reaction optimization algorithm (ImNROA), dynamically learns optimal routing paths to reduce end-to-end delay and energy consumption by avoiding the void area.This unified approach can effectively mitigate void-induced disruptions while balancing energy efficiency, extending the network lifetime, and improving the quality of service. Extensive simulations demonstrated that our model outperformed existing methods, reducing delay by up to 7%, while taking the number of nodes as 10, the delays of the IR2P (intelligent reinforcement learning routing protocol with integrated power-control), HMERP (hybrid message encoding-based routing protocol), ROAR (resource-optimized adaptive routing), VAHR (void-aware hybrid routing), and the proposed ImNROA-DBRAMADDPG were 0.8948%, 0.8639%, 0.84533%, 0.80878%, and 0.78594%, respectively, ensuring more stable data delivery in complex underwater scenarios.These advancements contribute to the state of the art by offering robust routing strategies capable of dynamically adapting to underwater environmental challenges and void formations. The findings provide potential implications for designing resilient and energy-efficient UASNs, paving the way for improved real-time underwater monitoring and secure acoustic communication systems. These findings pave the way for more reliable, sustainable, and intelligent underwater sensor networks, with significant implications for real-time marine exploration, defense, and environmental monitoring.

title: Research on an Improved Reconstruction Approach for Local Transmission Imaging in TGS
abstract: Tomographic gamma scanning is a nondestructive γ-ray measurement technique that utilizes computed tomography–based reconstruction methods to analyze the internal distribution of radioactive waste materials. To address the insufficient reconstruction accuracy of local regions under sparse-angle transmission measurement conditions, a geometry-guided global-to-local adaptive reconstruction method is proposed in this study.A surface layer voxel model of a radioactive waste container was established according to the practical configuration of low- and intermediate-level radioactive solid waste steel containers. The surface region was divided into 25 square voxel grids, with each a voxel size of 12 × 12 cm. Concrete filling material was placed at the 16th voxel position, and two models were constructed, in which the concrete occupied one-ninth and one-half of the initial voxel volume, respectively.Based on the source-detector scanning geometry, a geometric relationship X = H-2W was introduced to determine the minimum voxel partition length and the required number of subdivisions in the local region of interest. The Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)–Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) reconstruction framework was employed to reconstruct sparse-angle transmission projection data and improve the transmission image quality. Monte Carlo simulations were performed to validate the proposed reconstruction framework.The results demonstrated that under sparse-angle sampling conditions, the OMP method produces relatively poor reconstruction performance, with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) values of approximately 30 and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) values of around 0.6. In contrast, the ADMM-OMP framework effectively improved the reconstruction results, achieving PSNR values close to 40 and SSIM values close to 1, thereby improving the quality of the reconstructed transmission images.Finally, the global reconstructed image and the locally refined reconstruction results were fused, effectively alleviating the degradation of local reconstruction quality caused by the filling material occupying only a small fraction of the initial voxel in the region of interest.

title: Application of Nuclear Technology in Agriculture and the Role of Isotopes in Increasing Productivity, Food Security, and Sustainable Development in Türkiye
abstract: Nuclear technology has emerged as an important scientific approach for improving agricultural productivity, strengthening food security, and supporting sustainable development. However, despite the increasing global use of isotopes and irradiation techniques in agriculture, there is limited comprehensive research focusing on their applications, benefits, and future potential in Türkiye. Therefore, this study was carried out to examine the role of nuclear technology and isotope applications in Turkish agriculture, particularly in areas such as food irradiation, pest control, soil and water management, crop improvement, and sustainable resource utilization. The study was conducted using a qualitative and comparative review methodology based on scientific literature, international reports, institutional publications, and recent case studies related to nuclear applications in agriculture and food systems. Relevant studies from organizations such as the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), and recent international academic publications were systematically analyzed to evaluate current practices and developments in Türkiye and other countries. The analysis demonstrates that isotope and irradiation technologies contribute significantly to increasing agricultural productivity, improving fertilizer and water-use efficiency, reducing post-harvest losses, extending food shelf life, and decreasing dependence on chemical pesticides. Furthermore, the findings indicate that Türkiye has made notable progress in integrating nuclear techniques into agriculture through collaborations among universities, TENMAK, FAO, and IAEA. Nevertheless, challenges such as limited infrastructure, public awareness, regulatory development, and investment capacity still remain. The study concludes that nuclear and isotope technologies can play a strategic role in achieving sustainable agriculture and long-term food security in Türkiye. It is recommended that Türkiye strengthen interdisciplinary research, expand international cooperation, improve regulatory frameworks, and invest in scientific infrastructure and public awareness programs to support the safe and effective application of nuclear technologies in agriculture.

title: Selecting a project-delivery structure for Indonesia's first nuclear power plant: an expert AHP-weighted anchored-rating analysis of the bankability–strategic-control trade-off
abstract: Indonesia's energy policy and supply plan include nuclear generation, shifting attention from adoption to delivery. This study evaluates five case-anchored delivery configurations against 14 criteria covering ownership, contractual risk allocation, strategic national value, and financing feasibility, using a hybrid AHP-weighted anchored-rating model: 19 purposively selected Indonesian experts derived criterion weights by pairwise comparison and rated each configuration on an anchored nine-point scale; each respondent's weights and ratings were combined before aggregation. All 95 pairwise matrices met CR ≤ 0.10 under software-enforced consistency requirements, whereas agreement on dimension priorities was weak (Kendall's W = 0.187). Within this panel and under the administered profiles, a host-majority public–vendor joint venture scored highest (0.710), ahead of a state-utility configuration (0.638); its margin arose from perceived bankability, construction-risk allocation, and funding access, not from strategic national value, the largest-weighted dimension (34.4%). Priority heterogeneity alone reversed the group choice for no respondent; assessment heterogeneity reversed it for five. A1 led in over 98% of resampling and weight-variation draws, but the lead reversed when its seven contracting and financing ratings were lowered together by more than about 1.2 points. Newcomer delivery choices should weigh the risk bearer's control rights, exposure, and loss-absorption capacity, not nominal allocation alone.

title: Response Characteristics and Interference Evaluation of RAD7 Radon Measurement within 50,000 ppm CO2 Concentration Threshold
abstract: RAD7 is a core instrument for geological onsite radon measurements. When measuring the exhalation rate of radon from surface soil using closed accumulation chambers, concurrently exhaled carbon dioxide accumulates within the chamber. Similarly, during in-situ degassing for water-borne radon extraction, high concentrations of carbon dioxide in water are released together with radon. Under these conditions, CO 2 concentrations typically reach tens of thousands of ppm. To evaluate this conventional field concentration range's impact on RAD7, this study focused on CO 2 interference below 50000 ppm, established a closed-loop circulation experimental system with a dual-machine parallel comparison function. RAD7-4101 acted as the reference instrument measuring CO 2 -free radon; RAD7-4103 acted as the experimental instrument, undergoing six dynamic tests across five CO 2 gradients (10000 – 50000 ppm). Paired-ratio analysis revealed an overall negative offset but no statistically detectable dependence on CO 2 concentration, consistent with the small response predicted by existing models. At 50,000 ppm, the projected incremental interference could not be statistically resolved within the experimental precision, indicating no detectable concentration-dependent CO 2 -induced suppression under the present conditions.

title: Experimental Optimization of Filler Geometry for Vacuum Leak Mitigation in 200 MHz RFQ Section Brazing
abstract: Vacuum integrity is critical in the fabrication of radio-frequency quadrupole (RFQ) structures for high-intensity proton accelerators. This study investigated vacuum leak issues observed after section brazing of a 200 MHz RFQ at the Korea Multi-purpose Accelerator Complex (KOMAC) through experimental optimization of filler geometry. Specimen experiments were conducted to evaluate the effects of filler inclination angle and layout on the flow and redistribution behavior of molten Ag72Cu28 filler metal during high-vacuum brazing. The results showed that filler inclination angle strongly affects capillary-driven flow and gravity-induced redistribution. An effective inclination angle range of 15°–45° was identified, with 15° exhibiting the strongest preferential redistribution toward the critical vacuum seal area. Accordingly, 15° was selected for RFQ fabrication considering both filler redistribution and practical constraints, including bolt-hole interference, groove-machining space, and re-brazing accessibility. A ring-shaped filler layout was also introduced around bolt regions to reduce local filler deficiency and improve sealing continuity. The optimized design was validated through X-ray CT analysis and helium leak testing, demonstrating satisfactory vacuum integrity in the specimen experiments. The optimized layout was subsequently applied to full-scale RFQ section brazing. The fabricated RFQ sections exhibited satisfactory brazing appearance and satisfied the vacuum leak criterion of less than 1 × 10 -9 torr·L/s. These findings provide practical guidelines for controlling filler flow during large-scale vacuum brazing of RFQ structures.

title: F-MNet: flux-modulated network for radial power prediction of space reactors
abstract: Rapid and accurate prediction of radial power distribution is crucial for the design and operation of space nuclear reactors. However, traditional Monte Carlo methods incur prohibitively high computational costs, while conventional data-driven surrogate models face severe overfitting and insufficient generalization capabilities under small-sample and data distribution shift conditions. Addressing the problem of radial power prediction for rod-controlled space reactors, this paper proposes F-MNet (Flux-Modulated Network), a physics-informed neural network architecture. F-MNet employs the Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) mechanism to take the core-average neutron flux as a conditioning signal and dynamically adjust hidden-layer feature transformations, thereby learning the nonlinear sensitivity function of local assembly power with respect to flux—a relationship intrinsically constrained by the control rod differential worth. To evaluate the extrapolation performance under small-sample conditions, four dataset partitions with distinct characteristics of control rod position distributions were constructed. Ablation experiments demonstrate that F-MNet consistently outperforms all baseline models (Plain MLP, Res + FiLM, Res Only) across all partition schemes. Notably, in the challenging extrapolation scenario Case 1, F-MNet increased the R 2 from 0.4540 for Plain MLP to 0.9429, with the MAE, RMSE, and MAPE all reduced to approximately one-third. Furthermore, a cross-criticality case experiment was conducted, spanning subcritical (keff ≈ 0.62) to supercritical (keff ≈ 1.05) states, where the maximum relative deviation for all assemblies remained below 1.55%, further validating the engineering applicability of the model. The aforementioned results indicate that F-MNet is an efficient, accurate, and physically consistent model framework, providing a reference design paradigm for surrogate models dealing with small-sample and data distribution shift scenarios.

title: Experimental investigation on the thermal-hydraulic performance of an air–water parallel passive residual heat removal system
abstract: To enhance the safety and long-term cooling performance of passive residual heat removal systems (PRHRS) in offshore floating nuclear power plants, an air–water parallel passive residual heat removal system (AWPRHRS) is proposed and experimentally investigated. The system combines an air-cooled heat exchanger (AHX) and a water-cooled heat exchanger (WHX) in parallel, enabling efficient redistribution of thermal loads under varying heat conditions and reducing reliance on stored cooling water. The experimental facility was designed to evaluate key operational characteristics, including pressure response, natural circulation behavior, and thermal–hydraulic performance. Results demonstrate that the AWPRHRS can maintain high heat removal capacity under early-stage high heat load and achieve stable, long-term cooling without excessive water consumption. Under heat loads ranging from 35 to 45 kW, the system reaches a quasi-steady-state pressure of 0.65–0.66 MPa, while the air-cooled subsystem consistently carries approximately 37% of the total flow. The AWPRHRS effectively integrates the advantages of water- and air-cooled subsystems, providing both rapid initial decay heat removal and reliable long-term operation in the freshwater-limited OFNP environments.

title: Reliability-assessed machine learning for high flux flow regime classification
abstract: Thermal-hydraulic systems in nuclear engineering require reliable monitoring, accurate characterization and models capable of handling nonlinear, time-dependent behavior. High-void-fraction multiphase flows introduce significant diagnostic challenges, as the chaotic, nonlinear nature of interfacial transitions makes conventional modeling and rigid thresholding approaches less practical. This study develops a diagnostic framework for classifying annular gas–liquid flow sub-regimes using centerline conductivity probe measurements. Continuous experimental runs were partitioned into short temporal segments, with feature vectors constructed from volumetric, frequency-domain and morphological characteristics to represent the geometric structure of the flow. Four supervised learning architectures, K-nearest neighbors (KNN), support vector machines (SVM), random forest (RF) and gradient boosted trees (GBT), were evaluated. Feature selection reduced the initial six-feature configuration to an optimal three-feature subset, improving classification performance across most architectures. The RF model achieved the best overall results, with a macro F1 score of 0.9263 at the local segment level and perfect balanced accuracy under global run-level majority voting. Probabilistic evaluation using expected calibration error (ECE), maximum calibration error (MCE) and Brier scores confirmed that the RF model produced the most reliable confidence estimates among all evaluated classifiers. Overall, the study shows that machine learning can be applied to flow characterization problems to address challenges that traditional methods handle poorly. The results also highlight the importance of understanding model behavior, not just predictive accuracy, through analysis of evaluation methodology and calibration of predicted probabilities.

title: Multi-objective optimization of thermo-hydraulic performance for dimpled–protruded tubes of an intermediate heat exchanger in SCO2 gas fast reactor using machine learning and NSGA-II
abstract: The thermo–hydraulic performance of heat exchangers is governed by coupled interactions among geometry, flow conditions, and fluid properties. This study develops a hybrid framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), machine learning (ML) and multi-objective optimization framework to predict and optimize the thermo-hydraulic and exergy performance of supercritical CO 2 (SCO 2 ) flowing through dimpled-protruded tubes (DPTs) for intermediate heat exchangers in SCO 2 gas-cooled fast reactors. A CFD dataset comprising 504 cases was generated by varying Reynolds number ( Re ), Prandtl number ( Pr ), diameter of dimple-protrusion ( d / D ), and dimple-protrusion orientation parameter ( θ / ω ). Random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGB), and K-nearest neighbours (KNN) models were developed to predict Nusselt number ( Nu ), Poiseuille number ( fRe ), performance evaluation criterion ( PEC ), and exergy efficiency ( η W - S ). All models demonstrated good agreement with CFD results, with XGB achieving the highest predictive accuracy, followed by RF. At Re = 10 , 000 , d / D = 0.15 , and θ / ω = 0.33 , increasing Pr from 0.84 to 1.30 increased Nu by 56 % and PEC by 10 % . Increasing d / D from 0.10 to 0.25 enhanced Nu by 68 % but reduced PEC by 16 %, demonstrating the trade-off between heat-transfer enhancement and hydraulic performance. The best-performing XGB surrogate was coupled with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) to simultaneously maximize Nu and η W - S while minimizing fRe . The resulting Pareto-optimal solutions identify parameter combinations balancing heat-transfer enhancement, exergy performance, and hydraulic losses. The proposed CFD–ML–MOOP framework provides an efficient data-driven approach for the thermo-hydraulic design and optimization of advanced heat exchangers for next-generation nuclear energy systems.

title: LUT anchored target source calibration for critical heat flux prediction under source shift
abstract: The public NUREG derived set of 24,283 critical heat flux (CHF) measurements from 60 dryout dominated sources is studied under source shift. The tabulated outlet quality reconstructs the measured CHF from the heat balance (correlation 0.99989) and is excluded as target leakage. Under a leave one source out protocol the leakage safe model reaches 23.2 percent error and an inlet solved 2006 Groeneveld look up table 21.2 percent. A zero shot conformal interval gives a pooled coverage of 0.916 but source conditional coverage as low as 0.40 on biased sources, for the learned model and the table alike. A backbone agnostic calibration is proposed in which a few labelled target points correct a multiplicative bias and recalibrate an empirical conformal interval. A strict split protocol that separates adaptation from calibration restores near nominal empirical source conditional coverage with twenty to thirty target points, a cross conformal variant with about ten. Anchored on the look up table the calibration reaches about eleven percent error with the sharpest intervals, an in sample figure because the table was derived from this working set; re-deriving the table with the source held out costs about three points, and held out analogues anchor the calibration at seventeen to nineteen percent, near the learned backbone. All coverage values are empirical. The budget is stable over fifty target draws and under grouping by laboratory or network, but coverage falls to 0.83 to 0.93 when the labelled points cover only one mass flux or pressure block.

title: Design and thermal–hydraulic analysis of a directly heated test facility simulating plate type fuel with narrow rectangular channel for nuclear research reactors
abstract: Nuclear research reactors often use plate type fuel assemblies where coolant is passed through a set of narrow rectangular channels to transfer the heat from the reactor core. The channel gap between fuel plates strongly influences hydraulic resistance, fuel temperature, and the available margin to boiling, making it one of the key design parameters governing reactor safety during normal operation, anticipated operational occurrences, and accident conditions. This paper presents the design and development of the Heat-transfer Experiment Loop for Plate geometry (HELP), an out-of-pile test facility built to reproduce the thermal–hydraulic behaviour of plate-type fuel assemblies for research reactors. The facility employs a directly heated Inconel-625 test section with channel gaps of 1.7 mm, 1.8 mm, 2.0 mm, 2.2 mm and 2.4 mm, covering a large range of narrow gaps commonly adopted in research reactors. A steady-state design framework was established predicting hydraulic and thermal performance of a Directly Heated Test Facility simulating narrow rectangular channels. Pressure drop, wall temperature, heat-transfer coefficient, axial temperature distribution, and margin to onset of nucleate boiling (ONB) were evaluated using established friction-factor and heat-transfer correlations, including Shah-London, Blasius, Petukhov, Gnielinski, Dittus-Boelter, Sudo, and the SULTAN-JHR closures proposed by Ghione et al. The comparison highlights the variation among available correlations and defines the expected operating envelope of the facility. The resulting framework provides the theoretical basis for subsequent experimental measurements for validation of CFD simulations for narrow rectangular cooling channels representative of plate-type fuel for research reactors.

title: Adaptive coupling of transport and depletion using the neutronically weighted inventory deviation (NWID) metric
abstract: Most depletion engines solve transport at every depletion interval (fully transport-coupled depletion), this is the highest-fidelity option but impractical for many-interval histories. Some engines also offer a cheaper transport-independent mode that loses accuracy as the spectrum drifts. This paper introduces adaptive coupling as a new option that applies to both within-interval and across-interval depletion problems, triggering transport recalculation only when the Neutronically Weighted Inventory Deviation (NWID) tracking metric exceeds a user-defined tolerance. NWID quantifies inventory drift weighted by neutronic importance and is computed after each depletion interval at negligible cost. Demonstrations on PWR and SFR pin cells depleted at an irregular schedule to 45 and 131 MWd/kg, respectively, show that end-of-life baseline NWID differs by an order of magnitude between the two systems (145% for the PWR versus 14% for the SFR), mirroring the gap in their fully independent inventory errors and consistent with the spectral rigidity of fast systems. At 3% NWID tolerance simulations for both cases, the PWR recovers 0.61% maximum actinide error, 0.58% maximum fission product error, and - 45 pcm k eff deviation throughout the depletion history all relative to the fully coupled reference. While the SFR achieves 0.11% actinide error, 0.10% fission product error, and a k eff deviation of only - 19 pcm. Benchmarking results presented above were achieved while reducing the number of transport solves by 2.3 x and 14.3 x for PWR and SFR, respectively, with proportional reductions in runtime.

title: Can small modular reactors clear the cost screen for Greek noninterconnected islands: A benchmark screening assessment against oil based supply with illustrative renewable storage evidence
abstract: Greek noninterconnected islands remain economically distinctive because several still depend on autonomous oil based generation while facing pressure to decarbonize through renewables, storage, and interconnections. This article addresses a limited screening question. Do small modular reactors (SMRs) sit above or below the regulator documented cost of continued autonomous island supply, and how should that result be positioned against alternative decarbonization pathways. Using Greek regulatory data, peer reviewed SMR cost anchors, and an eighteen scenario levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) matrix for a 300 MWe proxy unit, the study identifies a central benchmark of 193.57 EUR per MWh and scenario results of 74.7 to 157.9 EUR per MWh. This favorable outcome holds only under the high technical availability assumed as a plant parameter. When Scenario S1 is translated into a more realistic island utilization of 40 to 50 percent, cost rises toward the benchmark, reaching about 187.9 EUR per MWh at 40 percent once the illustrative adders are applied. The discussion adds an illustrative comparison drawn from verified Greek island studies of photovoltaic and storage performance, presented as directional evidence that is not directly commensurate with plant level SMR LCOE. The article does not establish deployment feasibility or superiority over renewable systems with storage. It indicates only that SMRs cannot be excluded on cost screening grounds when the counterfactual is oil based island generation, while the margin narrows sharply under realistic low island utilization.

title: Optimization of the Heat Transfer Model for Superheated Steam Condensation Inside Tubes and Its Evaluation with the SPACE Code
abstract: This study focuses on condensation heat transfer of superheated steam inside tubes of once-through steam generators, which are utilized in various small modular reactors (SMRs). This work specifically investigates innovative SMR (i-SMR) and its passive auxiliary feedwater system (PAFS). The primary objective is to implement an optimized heat transfer model for superheated steam condensation into the Safety and Performance Analysis Code for Nuclear Power Plants (SPACE) code and subsequently validate it. To achieve this, a review of previous studies on superheated steam condensation heat transfer inside tubes was conducted to identify the best existing model for the PAFS operating conditions. The model identified from the literature review was first implemented in the SPACE code and evaluated against relevant experimental data. This evaluation revealed a key weakness, as the model underpredicted heat transfer in the high-superheat region. To address this shortcoming, an optimized model was developed by improving the single-phase forced convection heat transfer correlation for superheated steam based on a previous experimental study. This optimized model was subsequently implemented in the SPACE code. Validation calculations confirmed that the optimized model offers significantly improved prediction accuracy, especially in the high-superheat region, establishing it as the final model for the i-SMR PAFS.
title_ko: 스페이스 코드로 튜브 내부의 과열된 스팀 응축을 위한 열전달 모델 최적화 및 평가

title: Rate kinetics determination of cerium oxides conversion used as surrogate of specific heavy metal for process development
abstract: Specific heavy metal (SHM) nitrates generated during the back end of the nuclear fuel cycle are typically converted to metal oxalates using oxalic acid, followed by calcination to produce the metal oxides. Cerium was employed as actinide surrogate to investigate continuous precipitation and thermal decomposition relevant to process development and preliminary equipment design. A cerium nitrate solution containing 20 g/l Ce in 1M HNO 3 and 1M oxalic acid continuously fed to precipitator at a volumetric flow rate ratio of 3:1. The resulting cerium oxalate precipitate filtered using stainless steel filter and subjected to thermal analysis. Thermogravimetric and differential thermogravimetric analysis were performed from 303 - 1173K at heating rates of 5–25 K/min under inert atmosphere. Three distinct thermal decomposition stages were identified, corresponding to dehydration and two successive decomposition steps leading to CeO 2 formation. Apparent kinetic parameters for the individual stages were evaluated using nonisothermal Kissinger analysis. The experimentally observed mass losses were compared with theoretical values derived from the proposed decomposition steps. The results provide quantitative thermal and apparent kinetic information for cerium oxalate decomposition and establish an experimental basis for further mechanistic, heat & mass-transfer, and scale-up studies toward continuous drying and calcination of SHM oxalates.
title_ko: 공정 개발을 위한 특정 중금속의 대용으로 사용되는 세륨 산화물 전환율 동역학 측정

title: Observations regarding the construction of multipoint kinetics models from observational data
abstract: The multipoint kinetics (MPK) equations extend point kinetics models by tracking neutron populations in lumped reactor regions, offering improved spatial resolution at modest computational cost. However, determining the coupling coefficient matrix $K$ from transient data remains an open problem without established experimental procedures. This work provides some commentary on the task of recovering $K$ from observable forward flux measurements during reactor transients. Analytical solutions to the Kobayashi MPK formulation in the case of no precursors and with a single precursor family are derived in spectral form, enabling a mathematically rigorous investigation of eigenmode behavior and parameter observability. Coupling coefficient recoverability is investigated using modal sensitivity analysis and the Hessian condition number of the spectral recovery problem. The inclusion of delayed neutron precursors delays this eigenmode divergence but may be insufficient for enabling practical recovery of $K$ in many scenarios. In conclusion, capturing the behavior of nondominant eigenmodes without oversampling the dominant eigenmode is critical to the recoverability of $K$ through transient data.

title: High-efficiency 160-way cavity combiner: 170 kW CW validation for the IFMIF-DONES RF Power System
abstract: Solid-state (SS) amplification has become a compelling alternative to vacuum-tube technology for mid-range radiofrequency (RF) power systems, particularly at frequencies below a few hundred megahertz. This is the case of the RF Power System of IFMIF-DONES (International Fusion Materials Irradiation Facility – DEMO (DEMOnstration power plant) Oriented Neutron Source), composed of 56 RF Stations at 175 MHz based on SS technology. IFMIF-DONES is one of the key facilities of the European roadmap towards fusion electricity, necessary for the validation and qualification of the materials capable of withstanding the harsh conditions inside future fusion reactors. Nevertheless, achieving high power with SS technology requires combining the output of many transistor-based amplifier modules. Resonant cavity combination offers a compact and highly efficient single-step alternative to conventional corporate schemes. This work presents the latest validation campaign of the 160-input 175 MHz resonant cavity combiner developed for the IFMIF-DONES prototype SS RF Station. The device has been experimentally tested in continuous-wave (CW) mode up to 170 kW, extending previous validation experiments and providing new insight into the thermal behavior, efficiency evolution, and tuning characteristics of the system. The results confirm the suitability of resonant cavity combination for high-power SS RF sources and represent a significant step toward the full-power validation required for IFMIF-DONES.

title: An Intelligent Quality Assurance Pipeline for Large-Scale Personal Dosimetry Services Using Unsupervised Machine Learning-Based Anomaly Detection on Multi-Element TLD Readouts
abstract: Large-scale national personal dosimetry programs require stringent data quality assurance (QA) to prevent false exposure reports. Traditional QA relies on manual review or scalar thresholds, which fail to detect multi-dimensional anomalies. This paper presents an intelligent QA pipeline evaluating six unsupervised machine learning models against physics-grounded reference labels. We compiled a unified dataset of 14,732 records by programmatically matching raw reader outputs with dose spreadsheets (2024–2026), recovering 8,487 missing barcodes at a 99.1% matching rate via floating-point response fingerprinting. Evaluation against 379 physical anomalies proved that Isolation Forest achieved the highest performance (F1 = 0.580 at 1.5% contamination; F1 = 0.743 and Recall = 0.744 at 2.85% contamination), significantly outperforming One-Class SVM, Local Outlier Factor, and Elliptic Envelope (pairwise McNemar's tests with continuity correction, p < 0.001). Feature ablation confirmed that combining element shares, ratios, and operational metrics maximizes detection for Isolation Forest, while sensitivity analysis proved stable performance. The consensus intersection model yielded an operational precision of 0.592. This pipeline demonstrates the feasibility of integrating unsupervised learning into routine radiation protection workflows to safeguard national occupational dose registries.

title: Analysis of synergistic transport characteristics and selection of key nuclides for insoluble fission products in molten salt reactors
abstract: In liquid-fueled Molten Salt Reactors (MSRs), the non-uniform distribution of insoluble fission products (IFPs) significantly affects source term characterization, decay heat evaluation, and reactor safety. However, the single-atom transport assumption for IFP migration becomes invalid under high-power operations due to significant particle agglomeration. To clarify the relative importance of IFPs across various physical effects and alleviate computational bottlenecks in multiphysics simulations, this study evaluates the evolution characteristics of IFPs in a 150 MWth MSR under a conservative bounding accumulation assumption. By quantitatively screening four macroscopic physical parameters—mass deposition, radioactivity, decay heat, and core neutron absorption—using a hybrid cutoff criterion, this study reduces hundreds of dynamically evolving isotopes to a core inventory of 24 key nuclides. This reduction preserves over 95% of these original system's core physical features characteristics while significantly minimizing computational cost. Analysis of this reduced inventory reveals several critical transport phenomena: First, the macroscopic deposits are driven by a primary framework composed of high-yield, long-lived nuclides (primarily Mo, which accounts for >40%, alongside Ru). Second, a significant disparity between mass and activity/decay heat is observed, wherein trace high-risk nuclides (such as 95 Nb, 103 Ru) undergo coupled transport exclusively through attachment to these Mo Ru particles. Third, from a neutronics perspective, the spatial redistribution of long-lived solid poisons ( 103 Rh, 99 Tc) driven by particle migration induces non-negligible positive reactivity perturbations. Furthermore, decay chains (e.g., 95 Nb 95 Mo, 103 Ru 103 Rh) tightly couple early-stage thermal and safety issues with medium-to-long-term multiphase deposition and neutronics. In conclusion, the IFP transport characteristics and the 24-nuclide benchmark inventory established in this paper provide physically self-consistent inputs for future high-fidelity multiphysics coupled simulations, online purification system design, and surrogate material selection for non-radioactive experimental loops.
title_ko: 용융염 원자로에서 불용성 핵분열 생성물의 시너지 수송 특성 분석 및 주요 핵종 선택

title: Scattering-coupled adaptive source biasing for deep-penetration neutron arrival-spectrum calculations
abstract: Reliable neutron arrival spectra are needed for space radiation assessment and radiation protection, but deep-penetration Monte Carlo calculations often yield highly uneven uncertainties across energy groups. In analog Monte Carlo simulations, the nonuniform source spectrum and the energy-dependent transport behavior of neutrons can lead to relative uncertainties that differ by tens or even hundreds of times among arrival energy groups. To address this imbalance in arrival-spectrum uncertainties for deep-penetration transport, this study proposes a scattering-coupled adaptive source biasing (SC-ASB) method that uses a source-to-target response matrix to retain scattering-induced coupling from high-energy source neutrons to lower-energy arrival groups. The biased source distribution is derived by minimizing the sum of relative statistical errors (RSEs) subject to normalization and two-sided error-balance constraints, while the original source expectation is preserved by weight correction. Atmospheric neutron transport calculations showed that SC-ASB improved the relative-error distribution and increased computational efficiency. For a 15 km source height case, the figure of merit was 276 times that of analog simulation. Compared with uniform source biasing, SC-ASB showed better adaptability across source heights. In contrast to the WW variance-reduction method, SC-ASB provides more effective balancing of the RSEs across different energy groups. The method provides a variance-reduction framework for spectrum-resolved deep-penetration neutron transport.
title_ko: 깊은 침투 중성자 도달 스펙트럼 계산을 위한 산란 결합 적응 소스 바이어싱

title: Experimental study on discharge behavior in automatic depressurization system: overall discharge characteristics of the sparger
abstract: To investigate the high pressure two phase discharge characteristics of the sparger during the actual operation of automatic depressurization system (ADS), based on the discharge parameter conditions of the prototype sparger, the pressure oscillation behavior caused by the jet condensation of the racetrack orifices sparger was experimentally studied in this paper. The results show that under the condition of single phase discharge, the maximum oscillation increases first and then decreases with the increase of water temperature. With the increase of steam mass flow rate, it increases in the middle and high water temperature, and does not change significantly in the low water temperature. Under the condition of two phase discharge, when the water temperature is higher than 90 °C, the maximum oscillation increases with the increase of two phase mass flow rate and the decrease of equilibrium quality. Under single phase discharge conditions, the maximum oscillation appears in the condensation oscillation regime map, which is 123 kPa. Under the two phase discharge condition, it appears in the incomplete condensation regime map, which is 398 kPa. The maximum oscillation of the two phase condition is higher than that of the single phase condition. For the oscillation propagation law in the water tank, the maximum oscillation in the radial direction decreases with the increase of the distance from the sparger orifices, and the decrease amplitude decreases with the increase of the distance. In the axial direction, it shows a trend of decreasing first and then increasing.

title: A strongly connected component-based block solver for accelerated multi-node flowing-fuel depletion calculations
abstract: Spatially resolved depletion calculations for circulating-fuel systems couple nuclide transmutation with inter-node transport and generate large sparse spatial–nuclide matrices. Repeated factorization of the complex shifted systems can therefore dominate the computational cost of the Chebyshev rational approximation method (CRAM). This study develops a direct block solver based on strongly connected component (SCC) decomposition and implements it in MACT. The off-diagonal graph of the global depletion matrix is decomposed into SCCs and topologically ordered, transforming each CRAM shifted system into block lower-triangular form. Because the pole-dependent shifts affect only the diagonal entries, the same graph structure can be reused for all CRAM poles. The resulting block-forward solution retains all transmutation and migration couplings and is algebraically equivalent to the monolithic solution in exact arithmetic. The method was assessed for powered-node fraction, spatial scale, flow rate, zero-power decay, and a source-term history derived from the Molten-Salt Reactor Experiment (MSRE) model. For burnup calculations, the solver speedup increased with spatial scale and reached 420.8 for the 30-node case, whereas zero-power decay showed more modest acceleration. In the 30-node MSRE-derived source-term history comprising nine burnup and 15 post-shutdown decay steps, the unmerged SCC solver (SCC-RAW) achieved a solver speedup of 318.7; the maximum relative error among the reported aggregate inventories was 2.41 × 10 −10 at decay step 14, and the maximum all-nuclide decay-heat error was 5.87 × 10 −7 at decay step 15. The remaining runtime was dominated by factorization of the largest SCC. The method therefore provides an efficient structure-preserving solver for coupled depletion and transport calculations, although further treatment of dominant SCCs is required for larger systems.
